heroHeadline: Day 675: El Chinacate at Altiplano Prison — US Has 60-Day Window to Submit Extradition Request; Three FGR Fugitives Enter Day 30; 13-to-1 Chapitos vs Mayos Arrest Ratio Documented
heroSubtitle: 675 days of cartel civil war — May 29, 2026: Isaí Martínez Zepeda ('El Chinacate'), El Chapo's nephew and alleged Chapitos logistics operator, is held at Altiplano maximum-security prison (Almoloya de Juárez, State of Mexico) after a Mexican federal judge issued a provisional detention order with US extradition purposes on May 28. The United States has a 60-day deadline — approximately late July 2026 — to submit its formal extradition request. El Chinacate is the 14th cartel commander arrested since November 2024; an Infobae analysis (May 27) documented 13 of those 14 arrests targeted Chapitos — only 1 (Iván 'Mantecas,' January 18 in Badiraguato) was from La Mayiza, confirming the asymmetric security force targeting pattern. Three SDNY-indicted officials remain FGR fugitives entering Day 30: 'Cholo' Contreras Núñez, 'Tornado' Dionisio Hipólito, and 'El Comandante Juanito' Valenzuela Millán — who deserted his Culiacán police post at the war's start (Sep 2024) and faces the most serious individual charges including kidnapping resulting in death. Interpol red notices active (since May 21) against Rocha Moya and the three fugitives. Three of ten SDNY-indicted officials remain in US federal custody at Brooklyn MDC (Mérida Sánchez, Díaz Vega, Inzunza Cazárez). El Mayo Zambada sentencing (EDNY, 3rd postponement) set July 20; Ovidio (NDIL) July 27. La Mayiza ~90% territorial control; 13,300+ federal troops deployed under interim Governor Bonilla Valverde. Running conflict toll: ~2,425+ homicides (Noroeste) / 3,000+ (WSJ) since September 9, 2024; ~5,800 disappearances (NGO Sabuesos Unidas AC).
